A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NaLaFormer research despite the changed title. All pages, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, detection, segmentation, language-modeling, throughput and ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds Cityscapes, super-resolution, diffusion, Long Range Arena and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: V2 generalizes the fixed 0.5 offset in v1's query-power function to a tunable tau (v2 Eq. 5), with alternatives evaluated in Table 12. The underlying norm-direction decomposition, norm-dependent power, cosine/sine mapping and gated attention remain the same; expanded backbone descriptions do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: V2 adds Cityscapes segmentation; DIV2K-trained super-resolution evaluated on Set5, Set14, BSD100 and Urban100; ImageNet diffusion generation; and LRA tasks. These substantially extend task requirements and data coverage beyond v1's classification, detection, segmentation and language evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator sets change substantially: classification adds MetaLA, RAVLT and InLine variants; Mask R-CNN adds RAVLT/MAViT while dropping several earlier comparators; and ADE20K introduces SegFormer, VWFormer, EfficientViT and SegNeXt. InLine also joins the retained Swin-T attention comparison. New super-resolution, diffusion and LRA experiments introduce additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include the 8M-parameter XT configuration, super-resolution at x3/x4 with PSNR/SSIM and resource measurements, S/2 diffusion comparisons with generative metrics, and LRA sequences of 1K–4K tokens. Retained ImageNet, COCO and 15B-token language-training settings remain consistent across Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: V2 retains the original component ablation but adds XT backbone-component removals and tau/lambda sensitivity studies (Tables 11–12). Figure 4 replaces the raw dot-product illustration with comparisons against ReLU and 1+ELU. Additional evidence includes segmentation/super-resolution case studies and a PyTorch-versus-FLA implementation comparison (Table 13).

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, significance tests or explicit statistical uncertainty estimation. Existing norm–entropy plots retain their shaded trend bands, while new benchmark tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results, including XT accuracy of 79.1%, Cityscapes mIoU of 82.5/83.5%, LRA average accuracy of 61.19%, and super-resolution and diffusion outcomes. Retained NaLaFormer classification, COCO and language scores are unchanged. Among existing comparisons, VMamba-T's reported Mask R-CNN 1x box AP changes from 46.5 to 47.3; v1's separate SemanticFPN scores are omitted.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's coordinatewise PSE-concavity lemma and kernel-design theorem. Appendix A.1 extends the retained homogeneous-invariance calculation with Theorem A.2, an entropy-variation bound under multiplicative feature-map bounds, followed by a nonlinear/log-normal derivation. This substantially changes the formal assumptions and theoretical support, rather than merely relocating proofs.

C1.justification: V2 expands the headline contribution to state-of-the-art performance and practical long-sequence effectiveness, explicitly claiming 92.3% super-resolution memory savings and LRA leadership. Its conclusion strengthens v1's claim of a better performance–efficiency balance into consistently higher accuracy and better efficiency than existing linear-attention models.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of sharper segmentation boundaries and reconstruction textures, and attributes XT gains primarily to attention rather than auxiliary backbone components. New discussion addresses positional-encoding effects and deployment compatibility. The original limitation concerning costly text-to-image/video evaluation is retained in Appendix A.4.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies backbone block counts, channels, heads and the 3.5 MLP ratio (Table 8), and discusses FLA/fbi_la/Triton implementation. It adds task-specific implementation information and states that source code is in supplementary materials, although neither supplied PDF contains that code. V1's general GPU inventory is removed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against InLine's injectivity argument, MALA's treatment of magnitude neglect and MetaLA's recurrent approximation (Appendix A.5). It also identifies RALA as the vision-backbone basis and adds literature supporting the new application areas. These change substantive research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, method explanations and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The method is reorganized around query mapping, cosine direction and their unification; formal analysis and the original ablation move into expanded appendices. New future-work, implementation, visualization and full-table sections materially restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a new branded layout with colored headers and boxed definitions, updates the architecture diagram, and redraws the dot-product analysis. COCO tables are reorganized, RetinaNet moves to the appendix, and classification gains condensed/full displays. New task tables and segmentation, super-resolution and diffusion figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through explicit backbone configurations and strengthens the practical efficiency evidence with direct super-resolution latency/memory measurements and additional controls. These gains are moderated by stronger claims that overlook tradeoffs: Table 16 shows lower throughput and higher memory than PolaFormer despite higher average LRA accuracy. The new entropy bound also does not establish the claimed absence of negative norm–entropy correlation. The net improvement is useful but limited.
